questions.q: How does a random forest combine its trees?
options: It grows small trees in sequence, each fixing the last one's errors
It grows many deep trees independently on random samples and averages their predictions
It keeps only the single best tree
It replaces the trees with a linear model
questions.explain: Bagging averages independent trees, which cancels much of each tree's individual noise (variance reduction).

questions.q: Which statement best describes gradient boosting?
options: Trees are grown independently and averaged
It has no learning rate
It works only on text data
Small trees are added one at a time, each fitted to the errors the ensemble still makes
questions.explain: Boosting builds sequentially and mainly reduces bias, but because the trees depend on each other it can eventually overfit.

questions.q: In the churn experiment, how did XGBoost with untuned library defaults compare with the forest on clean labels?
options: It was clearly worse (about 0.797 versus 0.828 AUC)
It was clearly better
It was identical
It could not be scored
questions.explain: Aggressive defaults (learning rate 0.3, depth 6) overfit this small table. Boosting needs tuning or early stopping.

questions.q: When 20% of the training labels were flipped, which model held up best in the lesson?
options: The random forest with min_samples_leaf=20
XGBoost with library defaults
The tuned, shallow XGBoost (about 0.822 AUC)
All three fell by exactly the same amount
questions.explain: Untuned boosting fell to 0.729 and the forest to 0.811, while the shallow, regularized booster stayed near 0.822. Overfitting to noise is mostly a problem for deep, untuned boosting.

questions.q: What did the chart of held-out AUC versus number of trees show about forests and boosting?
options: Both improve forever as trees are added
The forest curve gets steadily worse with more trees
The forest flattens and stays stable, while a boosted model can peak and then decline, so it needs early stopping
Boosting was flat and the forest peaked early
questions.explain: Adding forest trees just settles the average, but boosting keeps fitting after its best round, so the tree count must be chosen carefully.
